newsitem.title: CAMEROON: Cameroon opposition parties discuss cooperation.
newsitem.headline: Cameroon opposition parties discuss cooperation.

text.p: Cameroon's two main opposition parties are discussing closer cooperation to ensure that they win all seven seats to be contested in parliamentary by-elections on August 3, party activists say.

A meeting last weekend between the leaders of the Social Democratic Front (SDF) and the National Union for Democracy and Progress (UNDP) has fueled speculation of a single opposition candidate for October's presidential election.

"The SDF and our party had decided to cooperate in order to cement our relationship which suffered some cracks at the beginning of the present session of parliament last month," one UNDP official told Reuters in Yaounde.

President Paul Biya, who took over from independence president Ahmadou Ahidjo in 1982, narrowly defeated SDF leader John Fru Ndi in a 1992 election run-off the opposition says was rigged. Biya's party easily won a May parliamentary election.

The seven vacant seats are in three constituencies where the supreme court cancelled May 17 parliamentary election results citing "severe irregularities and massive fraud" -- Mayo Banyo and Mayo Rey in the north and in Nde in Western Province.
The aim, the UNDP official said, was an electoral alliance to boost the UNDP tally in parliament from 13 to 15 -- the threshhold for it to claim parliamentary group status.

An SDP statement said Fru Ndi had invited UNDP leader Bello Bouba Maigari and other opposition parties for talks "to evaluate the socio-political situation... especially, after the bad experience of the recent legislative elections".
Biya's Cameroon People's Democratic Rally (RDPC) won 109 of the 180 national assembly seats on May 17, the SDF 43, the UNDP 13, four small parties the rest. The opposition cried foul.
